bib.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Dialogue Generation
bib.venue: Proceedings of the 2016 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP), pages 1192-1202

question: Can policy-gradient reinforcement learning with developer-defined rewards make neural chatbots model the long-term course of a dialogue rather than only the next turn?
hypothesis: Rewarding ease of answering, information flow and semantic coherence over simulated two-agent dialogues yields more interactive, diverse and sustained conversations than MLE seq2seq or mutual-information models.
contributions: A neural RL framework for open-domain response generation that simulates dialogue between two agents and optimises long-term developer-defined reward with policy gradient
Three heuristic rewards (ease of answering, information flow, semantic coherence)
Evaluation on diversity, simulated dialogue length and human judgement

method.summary: A 4-layer LSTM encoder-decoder with attention is trained with MLE on OpenSubtitles, refined with a mutual-information policy-gradient stage, then used to initialise an RL policy. Two copies converse for up to 5 simulated turns (5 candidates per step) and REINFORCE updates the policy on a weighted sum of three heuristic rewards, with curriculum over dialogue length.
method.task: open-domain neural dialogue response generation with RL

datasets.name: OpenSubtitles (supervised)
datasets.preprocessing: each turn is a target, concatenation of two previous sentences is the source

datasets.name: OpenSubtitles subset for simulation seeds
datasets.size: 10 million messages subset; 0.8 million sequences extracted
datasets.preprocessing: kept the 0.8M sequences with lowest likelihood of generating 'i don't know what you are taking about' so initial inputs are easy to respond to

models.name: SEQ2SEQ (LSTM encoder-decoder with attention)
models.architecture: 4-layer LSTM encoder-decoder with attention (Bahdanau et al., 2015)

models.name: Mutual information model
models.architecture: seq2seq policy fine-tuned by policy gradient on mutual information reward; also Li et al. 2015 n-best rerank variant

training.objective: Stage 1 MLE seq2seq; stage 2 REINFORCE on mutual information reward with learned baseline b; stage 3 REINFORCE on expected sum of rewards r = 0.25*r1 + 0.25*r2 + 0.5*r3 over simulated dialogue
training.optimizer: stochastic gradient descent for the policy updates; no learning rate stated

other.dull_response_list: 8 manually constructed dull turns (list not given in full)
other.curriculum_mi: MLE loss for first L tokens, REINFORCE for remaining T-L, L annealed to zero
other.curriculum_sim: simulate 2 turns, gradually increase; 5 turns at most; 5 candidate responses per step
other.baseline: separate neural model takes generated target and source and outputs baseline value

inference.decoding: beam search with beam size 10 for SEQ2SEQ and RL; mutual information model: n-best from p(t|s) reranked linearly with p(s|t)
inference.samples: 1 test pass over 1,000 inputs; no seeds or repeats stated

parameters.dialogue_end_rule: an agent produces a dull response (8-phrase rule list) or two consecutive utterances from the same agent share more than 80 percent of words

metrics.name: Simulated dialogue length
metrics.definition: number of turns before a dull response or an 80% overlap repeat, capped below 8

metrics.name: Diversity
metrics.definition: distinct unigrams and bigrams divided by total generated tokens (type-token ratio)

metrics.name: Pairwise human preference
metrics.definition: 3 crowd judges choose better output; win/lose/tie fractions of RL vs mutual information model

eval.protocol: Human: single-turn quality 500 items x 3 judges, single-turn ease to answer 500 items x 3 judges, multi-turn quality 200 simulated 5-turn conversations x 3 judges; no significance test details given though differences called significant. BLEU and perplexity deliberately not used.

results.quote: single reference BLEU scores for RL models, mutual information models and vanilla SEQ2SEQ models are respectively 1.28, 1.44 and 1.17.

limits: Hand-defined reward cannot cover what defines an ideal conversation; ideally rewards come from humans (Sec 5.2 discussion)
Only a very small number of candidates and simulated turns is affordable because cases grow exponentially
Dialogues can enter cycles longer than one turn (Table 6) because only limited history is considered
Model sometimes starts a less relevant topic; relevance vs non-repetition tradeoff
RL model has lower BLEU than the mutual information model
Dialogue-end detection uses rule matching over 8 dull phrases, with false positives and negatives
Reward-related and optimisation hyperparameters (learning rate, batch size, hidden size, steps, compute) are not reported; no code release stated

terms.definition: reward r1: negative length-normalised log likelihood, averaged over a list of 8 dull responses, of answering the generated turn with a dull response
